title: Arduino Code Basics
summary: Understand the complete structure of an Arduino sketch.

steps.title: Arduino Sketch Structure
steps.markdownContent: An Arduino sketch is written in C++. The two mandatory building blocks required in every sketch are `setup()` and `loop()`. Libraries (`#include`) and global variable declarations at the top are optional—you only include them when your sketch needs external drivers or shared data storage!

quickCheck.question: What is a function in programming?
options: A named reusable block of code that performs a specific job
A physical screw on the board
quickCheck.explanation: Functions package instructions under a single name so you can call them whenever needed!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Think of a function like a spell or recipe named makeToast(). Whenever you say makeToast(), it runs the steps!

quickCheck.question: Why do programmers break large programs into smaller functions?
options: To make code organized, easier to read, and reusable
quickCheck.explanation: Functions keep programs organized and allow code to be reused without duplicating lines!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Organizing toys into labeled bins makes them easy to find and play with again.

steps.title: Setup
steps.markdownContent: The `setup()` function runs exactly once when power is applied. It's used for configurations like `pinMode()`.

steps.title: Loop
steps.markdownContent: The `loop()` function runs repeatedly, forever. It contains the main behavior of your program, using functions like `digitalWrite()` and `delay()`.

steps.title: Compilation & Uploading
steps.markdownContent: Code is compiled (translated to machine instructions) and uploaded to the board via USB.

steps.title: IDE Lifecycle
steps.markdownContent: Watch the setup() and then loop() cycle.

steps.title: Knowledge Check
steps.markdownContent: Test what you learned about the sketch structure.

questions.question: How many times does `setup()` run?
questions.explanation: Setup runs once at startup to initialize settings.

questions.question: Where should you put code that needs to repeat continuously?
options: At the top of the file
questions.explanation: The loop() function repeats its contents indefinitely.

questions.question: What does compiling do?
questions.explanation: Compilation translates human-readable C++ into binary machine code.

questions.question: What is a global variable?
questions.explanation: Variables declared outside of functions are global and can be used anywhere in the sketch.
